notes: Writing a scene no longer means hunting for the asterisk key. In person mode adds a pencil button beside the composer: tap it and you are writing an action, tap it again and you are back to speech, so one message can carry a line, a gesture and another line without typing a single asterisk. It works mid-message rather than only at the start, because it opens and closes the description wherever the cursor happens to be — and the button lights up whenever the cursor sits inside one, so you can always tell which you are writing. A description left open is closed for you when you send, and one you opened and thought better of disappears instead of going out as a stray asterisk. Descriptions now read like a script rather than a smear: each one breaks onto its own line in the bubble, and the speech either side breaks too, with the spacing that used to separate them cleaned up so nothing sits indented. That applies to what the characters write as well as what you write, which is where most of the benefit is. The button stays out of the way in texting chats, where actions do not belong at all.
